subject: Model fit follow-up & prompt set request - Acme (next steps)
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Thanks for the demo - next steps for model fit & prompt collection

Hi Emily / Raj,

Thanks again for the call today - great to learn more about Acme's search summarization workflow and the failure cases you called out (long multi-doc threads, billing account IDs mixed with free text, and the low-confidence summaries for technical spec docs). As discussed, next steps from our side: 

- Recommend a short benchmark run across two model families we think fit your latency/cost targets: rw-gpt-7b-quant (fast + cheap) and rw-gpt-30b-std (higher quality for technical content).
- We'll run the benchmarks on a representative prompt set; can you share ~50 production prompts (and a few edge-case examples) by EOD Thu so we can prioritize?
- Attachments: I dropped a prompt-set template (acme_prompt_set_v1.xlsx) and our redaction guidance (redaction_guidance.pdf) to make sharing safe. Please redact or mask PII per the guidance - if you prefer, we can sign an additional DPA before you share raw logs.

On quality regressions: we will baseline current production outputs and run automated evals (ROUGE/EM/semantic-sim) and a small human pass on sampled cases. If we see regressions vs your baseline, we'll provide detailed diffs and recommended prompt edits.

Would Thu EOD for the prompts and a quick sync on Fri 10am PT work?

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
log@nwood.com | +1 415-555-0112

Attachments: acme_prompt_set_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet template), redaction_guidance.pdf (pdf)

Thanks Logan - that timeline works. A few quick clarifications: 

1) We can provide 50 prompts but many include customer names and account IDs. Per your redaction guidance, is replacing account IDs with [ACCOUNT_ID] ok?
2) For edge cases, we'll include: multi-doc threads >10 messages, code snippets (python/js), and legal language. 
3) Can you confirm what level of human review you do for the "small human pass" and whether that will require our reviewers?

Also looping Raj - he owns the integration side. We'll aim to upload the prompt file to the Drive link you shared by Thu EOD.

Best,

Subject: RE: Thanks for the demo - next steps for model fit & prompt collection

Hi team,

Quick note on the model/recommendation side from our evaluation team: 

- Initial benchmark plan: run per-prompt latency and quality on rw-gpt-7b-quant (q4_0 quant) and rw-gpt-30b-std. If latency for 30b exceeds your SLO on multi-doc threads, we'll also test rw-mistral-70b-quant as a middle ground.
- Metrics we'll produce: per-prompt token cost, median latency @p50/p95, semantic-similarity (embedding cosine), and a human-quality rubric (fluency/faithfulness/relevance).
- Redaction guidance reminder: please replace direct PII (names, emails, account_ids) with bracketed tokens like [NAME], [EMAIL], [ACCOUNT_ID]. Do not remove structural context (e.g., "Invoice # [ACCOUNT_ID] for project X") as we need that for model behavior.

For the human pass: our applied ML team will do an initial triage (15-20 samples) and request a short set of clarifying judgments from one Acme reviewer for borderline cases. We can coordinate reviewer access via a one-time SharePoint/Drive permission.

I attached a short checklist and the prompt-set template (acme_prompt_set_v1.xlsx).

Cheers,
Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa.co@redwood.ai

Attachments: checklist.txt (txt), acme_prompt_set_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)
